interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: The learner follows the conceptual sequence: one s orbital plus three p orbitals combine into four equivalent sp3 hybrids, which then orient as a tetrahedron rather than as opposite pairs

interactions.label: Show 109.5° guide
interactions.teaches: Every pair of final sp3 hybrid directions is separated by the tetrahedral angle, so the final geometry is not a cross, not three perpendicular p orbitals, and has no directly opposite large lobes
Rotating the final arrangement reveals that the four sp3 directions are genuinely three-dimensional tetrahedral vectors; the textbook-like drawing is only a projection of that 3D geometry
Hovering identifies individual orbitals and axes without crowding the p-orbital region, making clear which source orbital contributes to the four hybrids

demo_steps.title: Start with the atomic orbitals
demo_steps.narration: The source ingredients are one spherical 2s orbital and three mutually perpendicular 2p orbitals. The p-orbital labels are placed outside the lobes so the x, y, and z directions remain readable.

demo_steps.title: Hybridization produces four equal hybrids
demo_steps.narration: The long Hybridization arrow leads to four identical sp3 hybrid orbitals. Each preview hybrid has a large lobe and a smaller rear lobe, showing the asymmetric shape of a hybrid orbital.

demo_steps.title: The four hybrids point tetrahedrally
demo_steps.narration: The large gray downward arrow moves from the four preview hybrids to their final spatial arrangement. The four large lobes point toward the corners of a tetrahedron, not along two straight opposite axes.

demo_steps.title: See the complete source-style sequence
demo_steps.narration: The full diagram shows the textbook-style flow from 2s + three 2p orbitals, through hybridization, to the final tetrahedral sp3 geometry. Orbit the scene to confirm that the final 109.5° geometry is truly three-dimensional.

plan.geometry_notes: Use a mostly source-style schematic layout in world coordinates with +X screen-right, +Y screen-up, and +Z as depth/receding direction. Overall extents about X = -6.2 to +4.7, Y = -3.2 to +3.0, Z = -1.6 to +1.6. Left source group: place the 2s orbital at (-5.1, 1.55, 0), radius about 0.45, pale blue #79aee3, translucent. Put a black plus sign at (-4.35, 1.55, 0). Put the shared 2p center at (-3.25, 1.55, 0). Draw p_x as a dumbbell along local +X/-X, p_y along local +Y/-Y, and p_z along local +Z/-Z; each p lobe length about 0.55 from center, maximum radius about 0.22, with a thin black axis line extending to about 0.95 from center. Use warm p-lobe colors such as orange #f4a23a and gold #f2c14e, with slight transparency for the z-depth pair. Axis label placement must be uncluttered: x label just beyond the +X axis endpoint and slightly below it, y label above the +Y endpoint and slightly left, z label beyond the +Z/receding endpoint and offset upward/right so it does not sit on the lobe. Put the 2s label below the sphere and the 2p label below or just outside the p-orbital set. Horizontal Hybridization arrow: make it a distinct long arrow, not just a small arrowhead; shaft from roughly (-1.75, 1.55, 0) to (0.75, 1.55, 0), shaft thickness about 0.045 to 0.06, arrowhead length about 0.25, dark gray #555555, label 'Hybridization' centered above at Y about 1.9. Upper-right preview group: four isolated sp3 orbitals arranged as a clean 2×2 block or slight arc centered near (2.3, 1.55, 0), with centers approximately (1.75, 2.05, 0), (2.85, 2.05, 0), (1.75, 1.15, 0), (2.85, 1.15, 0). Each preview orbital is identical: large lobe pointing generally +X or slightly upper-right, length about 0.55, bulb radius about 0.22, color yellow-orange #f5b041; small rear lobe opposite, length about 0.22, radius about 0.10, pale blue #79aee3. Put an 'sp3' label near each preview but offset outward. Downward arrow: make it large and unmistakable between the preview group and final arrangement, centered near X = 2.3; shaft from about (2.3, 0.55, 0) down to (2.3, -0.45, 0), shaft thickness about 0.075 to 0.10, arrowhead length about 0.32, color medium gray #777777, with enough empty space around it that it reads as the source-style transition arrow. Final arrangement: central atom sphere at (2.3, -1.75, 0), radius about 0.14 to 0.18, dark gray #444444. The final four large sp3 lobe directions MUST be mathematically tetrahedral in 3D, with every pair separated by arccos(-1/3) = 109.471 degrees. A convenient direction set, before any whole-object rotation, is d0 = (0, 1, 0), d1 = (0.942809, -0.333333, 0), d2 = (-0.471405, -0.333333, 0.816497), d3 = (-0.471405, -0.333333, -0.816497). Use these or an equivalent rigidly rotated tetrahedral set; do not use ±X/±Y/±Z axes and do not create any directly opposite pair of large lobes. Orient the final object so the projection resembles the source: one lobe projects upward, one lower-right, and two lower-left/back/front with visible depth separation. Each final large lobe extends from the central atom about 1.05 to 1.20 units along its tetrahedral vector, maximum radius about 0.28, yellow-orange #f5b041; each small rear lobe extends only about 0.28 to 0.35 units along the opposite direction, pale blue #79aee3. If the angle guide is enabled, draw a thin dashed gray tetrahedron connecting the four large-lobe tips and show one to three visible 109.5° labels near arcs between representative direction pairs; all six pairwise directions are 109.471° even if not all labels are displayed.
plan.notes: Render orbitals as smooth ellipsoid or teardrop meshes, not as flat icons. The final tetrahedral arrangement should be built from normalized vector directions and then transformed as one rigid group, so the 109.471° separations are preserved while the projection matches the textbook view. Use label sprites or CSS2D labels with depth-aware offsets; p-axis labels should have collision-free fixed offsets rather than being attached exactly at lobe tips. In Full sequence mode, show all groups and both arrows; in the other view modes, fade or hide nonselected groups while keeping the camera framing stable. Use cylinders plus cones for the Hybridization and downward arrows so their shaft length and thickness are visibly source-like. The angle guide should be toggled independently and should not distort the tetrahedral geometry.

authoredPrompt: This figure illustrates the sp3 hybridization process as a stepwise transformation, moving from four distinct atomic orbitals on the left to four equivalent hybrid orbitals on the right and finally to the tetrahedral arrangement they collectively produce at the bottom. The upper-left section shows the four pre-hybridization atomic orbitals drawn individually on Cartesian axes: a spherical s orbital (blue), a px orbital (two-lobed, red and blue, oriented along the x-axis), a py orbital (two-lobed, oriented along the y-axis), and a pz orbital (two-lobed, oriented along the z-axis). A rightward arrow labeled "Hybridization" leads to four equivalent sp3 hybrid orbitals, each rendered as a prominent orange lobe with a small back-lobe, shown individually pointing in different directions; a downward arrow then labeled "Gives a tetrahedral arrangement" leads to a final diagram in which all four sp3 orbitals appear simultaneously, with their large lobes directed symmetrically toward the four corners of a tetrahedron at 109.5° with respect to each other. This figure demonstrates how the mathematical mixing of one s and three p orbitals destroys the original orbital distinctions and produces four energetically and geometrically equivalent sp3 hybrids that underpin the tetrahedral bond angles observed in molecules such as CH4, NH3, and H2O.
authoredInteractions: - Toggle individual atomic orbital contributions (s, px, py, pz) on and off: isolate each orbital and see its role in forming the tetrahedral hybrid
authoredContext:
The valence orbitals of an atom surrounded by a tetrahedral arrangement of bonding pairs and lone pairs consist of a set of four sp 3 hybrid orbitals . The hybrids result from the mixing of one s orbital and all three p orbitals that produces four identical sp 3 hybrid orbitals ( ). Each of these hybrid orbitals points toward a different corner of a tetrahedron.

The hybridization of an s orbital (blue) and three p orbitals (red) produces four equivalent sp 3 hybridized orbitals (yellow) oriented at 109.5° with respect to each other.

A series of three diagrams connected by a right-facing arrow that is labeled, “Hybridization,” and a downward-facing arrow labeled, “Gives a tetrahedral arrangement,” are shown. The first diagram shows a blue spherical orbital and three red, peanut-shaped orbitals, each placed on an x, y, z axis system. The three red orbitals are located on the x , y and z axes, respectively. The second diagram shows the same four orbitals, but they are now purple and have one enlarged lobe and one smaller lobe. Each lies in a different axis in the drawing. The third diagram shows the same four orbitals, but their smaller lobes now overlap to form a tetrahedral structure.

A molecule of methane, CH 4 , consists of a carbon atom surrounded by four hydrogen atoms at the corners of a tetrahedron. The carbon atom in methane exhibits sp 3 hybridization. We illustrate the orbitals and electron distribution in an isolated carbon atom and in the bonded atom in CH 4 in . The four valence electrons of the carbon atom are distributed equally in the hybrid orbitals, and each carbon electron pairs with a hydrogen electron when the C–H bonds form.

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: The learner sees the process as a transformation from one spherical s orbital plus three perpendicular p orbitals into four equivalent directional sp3 hybrids, and then into the shared tetrahedral geometry.

interactions.label: s contribution
interactions.teaches: The spherical s contribution is common to all four hybrids; it helps make the four resulting orbitals equivalent rather than preserving a directional p-only pattern.

interactions.label: px contribution
interactions.teaches: The px contribution separates hybrids into lobes with positive and negative x character, helping aim the tetrahedral set to the right and left.

interactions.label: py contribution
interactions.teaches: The py contribution separates hybrids along the diagonal y direction, showing that tetrahedral orientation needs a component outside the flat xz plane.

interactions.label: pz contribution
interactions.teaches: The pz contribution gives the hybrids vertical character, producing the upward and downward parts of the tetrahedral arrangement.
Rotating the figure reveals that the final four hybrid orbitals are arranged in three dimensions, not as a flat four-lobed drawing.

demo_steps.title: Start with separate atomic orbitals
demo_steps.narration: The left-side view shows the four starting orbitals separately: one spherical s orbital and three mutually perpendicular p orbitals. Their colors indicate opposite phases of the p lobes before hybridization.

demo_steps.title: Isolate one p contribution
demo_steps.narration: Turn off every contribution except pz. The vertical two-lobed character remains, showing that a single p orbital alone cannot produce four equivalent tetrahedral hybrids.

demo_steps.title: Combine all four contributions
demo_steps.narration: With s, px, py, and pz all enabled, the four combinations become equivalent sp3 hybrids. Each hybrid has one large directional lobe and a small back-lobe.

demo_steps.title: See the tetrahedral set
demo_steps.narration: When the four equivalent hybrids are placed at one atom, their large lobes point toward the corners of a tetrahedron. The angle between any pair of full hybrid directions should read as about 109.5 degrees.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use a compact axonometric chemistry-orbital style. Each small orbital panel should fit in a roughly 2.4 × 2.4 × 2.4 world-unit cube. Axis arrows in each panel span about 1.35 units from the origin: +X points screen-right, +Z points screen-up, and +Y is the receding diagonal up-right. Atomic s orbital radius ≈0.38 units, translucent blue #5f8fd6 with white highlight. Atomic p lobes are teardrop or ellipsoid lobes length ≈0.85 units and maximum radius ≈0.28 units, centered on opposite sides of the origin along the named axis; positive phase blue #5f8fd6, negative phase red/pink #e76f7a. The source layout places the four atomic orbitals as a 2×2 block: s upper-left, px upper-right, py lower-left, pz lower-right. The hybridization arrow is horizontal gray #8a8a8a, pointing right from the atomic block toward the hybrid block. In the Hybrid orbitals view, arrange four separate sp3 panels as a 2×2 block resembling the right half of the source: upper-left hybrid large lobe along +Z; upper-right large lobe mostly +X; lower-left large lobe mostly left/down/back; lower-right large lobe mostly downward/front. Each sp3 hybrid has a large orange/yellow lobe length ≈1.05 units, radius ≈0.34 units, plus a small back-lobe length ≈0.24 units and radius ≈0.10 units opposite the main direction. Use orange/yellow #f4a62a, highlight #ffe08a, edge/shadow amber #d98a12. In the final Tetrahedral arrangement view, all four hybrids share one origin and use normalized directions d1=(0,0,1), d2=(0.943,0,-0.333), d3=(-0.471,0.816,-0.333), d4=(-0.471,-0.816,-0.333), giving pairwise angles of arccos(-1/3)=109.47°. Draw large lobes outward along these directions with the same small opposite back-lobes. Faint gray guide lines #999999 extend slightly beyond each lobe tip. Hybrid formula to drive contribution toggles: h1=(s+px+py+pz)/2, h2=(s+px-py-pz)/2, h3=(s-px+py-pz)/2, h4=(s-px-py+pz)/2. Disabled contributions should be omitted from these sums and the resulting hybrid previews should become visibly incomplete or less tetrahedral; when all four toggles are enabled, show the canonical orange sp3 shapes.
interactionPlan.notes: Implement the three named view stages by showing one major layout at a time rather than displaying the entire textbook composite simultaneously. Use smooth shaded parametric lobe meshes or scaled metaball-like implicit surfaces; exact orbital probability density is less important than preserving phase, orientation, and relative lobe size. Contribution toggles should gray out or hide the corresponding atomic orbital in the Atomic orbitals view and should recompute or visually attenuate the corresponding term in the hybrid views. Keep axis labels as screen-facing text sprites. Add a subtle translucent overlap/gradient on lobes to resemble the source figure’s glossy textbook rendering.

discrepancies: The generated figure splits the source's single composite flow into separate stages; the default view shows only the starting atomic orbitals and a hybridization arrow without the hybrid or tetrahedral products visible.

The axis projection is noticeably different from the source: x is drawn diagonally rather than horizontally and the y direction often appears reversed/down-left, which changes the visual orientation of the p orbitals.
The atomic orbital panels are compressed and rearranged compared with the source, with the hybridization label/arrow intruding close to the p orbital panels.

The original shows the hybrid orbitals, downward arrow, and final tetrahedral arrangement as one connected layout, while the generated version isolates them behind controls and loses the visual continuity.
There are extra explanatory labels and UI contribution controls not present in the textbook figure, which make the result more like an interactive lesson than a faithful reproduction.
evaluation.notes: The main sp3 hybridization concept is represented with good interactive controls, but the projection, layout, and staged composition differ noticeably from the source figure.
action_items: Adjust the camera/projection so the x axis is horizontal, z is vertical, and y points diagonally upward as in the source.

demo_steps.title: Full transformation overview
demo_steps.narration: The default view matches the source figure as a full-page transformation: four starting atomic orbitals on the left, four equivalent sp3 hybrids on the right, and the final tetrahedral arrangement below. The arrows show the conceptual flow without adding extra non-source annotations.

demo_steps.title: Start with four distinct atomic orbitals
demo_steps.narration: Focus on the 2x2 atomic-orbital block. The s orbital is spherical, while px, py, and pz are directional p orbitals aligned with the horizontal x-axis, diagonal y-axis, and vertical z-axis.

demo_steps.title: Hybridization makes four equivalent orbitals
demo_steps.narration: Move to the hybrid-orbital block. After hybridization, the original distinction between s, px, py, and pz is replaced by four equivalent sp3 orbitals, each with one large directional lobe and one small back-lobe.

demo_steps.title: Equivalent hybrids point tetrahedrally
demo_steps.narration: Focus on the bottom arrangement. The four sp3 hybrids now share one origin and point toward the corners of a tetrahedron, giving the characteristic 109.5° separation.

plan.geometry_notes: Use an oblique textbook-style projection matching the source axes: +X maps horizontally to screen-right, +Z maps vertically upward, and +Y maps diagonally upward-right as the receding axis. No perspective convergence. In the full overview, place the atomic block on the upper-left and the hybrid block on the upper-right, with the final tetrahedral panel below the hybrid block. Use world coordinates with layout shifts mainly in X and Z, while each panel's local orbital depth uses Y. Overall full figure spans about X=-5.6 to +5.6, Z=-4.0 to +3.6, and local Y about -1.2 to +1.2. Each small orbital panel occupies about 1.8 X × 1.2 Y × 1.7 Z world units. Atomic panel centers: s at (-4.35, 0, 2.45), px at (-2.35, 0, 2.45), py at (-4.35, 0, 0.45), pz at (-2.35, 0, 0.45). Hybrid panel centers: h1 at (1.30, 0, 2.45), h2 at (3.30, 0, 2.45), h3 at (1.30, 0, 0.45), h4 at (3.30, 0, 0.45). Final tetrahedral panel center: (2.35, 0, -2.45), scaled about 1.25 times larger than the small panels. The rightward Hybridization arrow should run through the clear gap between blocks from approximately X=-0.90 to X=0.45 at Z=1.45, with its label above at Z=1.75; keep px and pz labels close to their panels so the arrow does not overlap them. The downward arrow should run from the hybrid block bottom center near (2.35, 0, -0.45) to the final panel top near (2.35, 0, -1.35), with the label Gives a tetrahedral arrangement placed to the right of the arrow. Axis arrows in every panel span about 0.75 units from the local origin; x is horizontal right, z vertical up, y diagonal up-right. Use black #111111 for axes and text, arrow gray #8a8a8a. s orbital: translucent blue sphere radius about 0.34, color #5f8fd6, opacity about 0.72. p orbitals: two glossy lobes along the named axis, each lobe length about 0.62 from origin and max radius about 0.24; positive lobe blue #5f8fd6 and negative lobe red/pink #e76f7a. Separate sp3 orbitals: large glossy orange lobe length about 0.82, max radius about 0.30, plus small opposite back-lobe length about 0.22 and radius about 0.09; color orange/yellow #f4a62a with highlight #ffe08a and darker edge #d98a12. In the individual hybrid block and in the final arrangement, use the same four tetrahedral directions, normalized: d1=(0,0,1), d2=(0.943,0,-0.333), d3=(-0.471,0.816,-0.333), d4=(-0.471,-0.816,-0.333). These give pairwise angles arccos(-1/3)=109.47°. Large tetrahedral lobes extend outward along d1-d4; small back-lobes point along -d1 through -d4. Keep only source-style labels visible by default: s, px, py, pz, sp3, x, y, z, Hybridization, and Gives a tetrahedral arrangement.
plan.notes: Default rendering must be the full composite overview, not an isolated stage. Focus modes should zoom or fade to the requested region while preserving the same oblique axis convention. Avoid extra contribution legends, equations, or explanatory callouts in the main view; show the 109.5° angle arc and correspondence highlighting only after click selection. Use screen-facing text sprites for labels, with p-subscript labels rendered as p_x, p_y, p_z if true subscripts are unavailable. Use smooth shaded parametric lobes or implicit-surface meshes; chemical-orbital recognizability and orientation are more important than exact wavefunction density. Provide a reset-to-source-view behavior after orbiting so the x-horizontal, z-vertical, y-diagonal default view is easy to recover.

plan.geometry_notes: Use a mostly source-style schematic layout in world coordinates with +X screen-right, +Y screen-up, and +Z as depth/receding direction. Overall extents about X = -6.2 to +4.7, Y = -3.2 to +3.0, Z = -1.6 to +1.6. Left source group: place the 2s orbital at (-5.1, 1.55, 0), radius about 0.45, pale blue #79aee3, translucent. Put a black plus sign at (-4.35, 1.55, 0). Put the shared 2p center at (-3.25, 1.55, 0). Draw p_x as a dumbbell along local +X/-X, p_y along local +Y/-Y, and p_z along local +Z/-Z; each p lobe length about 0.55 from center, maximum radius about 0.22, with a thin black axis line extending to about 0.95 from center. Use warm p-lobe colors such as orange #f4a23a and gold #f2c14e, with slight transparency for the z-depth pair. Axis label placement must be uncluttered: x label just beyond the +X axis endpoint and slightly below it, y label above the +Y endpoint and slightly left, z label beyond the +Z/receding endpoint and offset upward/right so it does not sit on the lobe. Put the 2s label below the sphere and the 2p label below or just outside the p-orbital set. Horizontal Hybridization arrow: make it a distinct long arrow, not just a small arrowhead; shaft from roughly (-1.75, 1.55, 0) to (0.75, 1.55, 0), shaft thickness about 0.045 to 0.06, arrowhead length about 0.25, dark gray #555555, label 'Hybridization' centered above at Y about 1.9. Upper-right preview group: four isolated sp3 orbitals arranged as a clean 2×2 block or slight arc centered near (2.3, 1.55, 0), with centers approximately (1.75, 2.05, 0), (2.85, 2.05, 0), (1.75, 1.15, 0), (2.85, 1.15, 0). Each preview orbital is identical: large lobe pointing generally +X or slightly upper-right, length about 0.55, bulb radius about 0.22, color yellow-orange #f5b041; small rear lobe opposite, length about 0.22, radius about 0.10, pale blue #79aee3. Put an 'sp3' label near each preview but offset outward. Downward arrow: make it large and unmistakable between the preview group and final arrangement, centered near X = 2.3; shaft from about (2.3, 0.55, 0) down to (2.3, -0.45, 0), shaft thickness about 0.075 to 0.10, arrowhead length about 0.32, color medium gray #777777, with enough empty space around it that it reads as the source-style transition arrow. Final arrangement: central atom sphere at (2.3, -1.75, 0), radius about 0.14 to 0.18, dark gray #444444. The final four large sp3 lobe directions MUST be mathematically tetrahedral in 3D, with every pair separated by arccos(-1/3) = 109.471 degrees. A convenient direction set, before any whole-object rotation, is d0 = (0, 1, 0), d1 = (0.942809, -0.333333, 0), d2 = (-0.471405, -0.333333, 0.816497), d3 = (-0.471405, -0.333333, -0.816497). Use these or an equivalent rigidly rotated tetrahedral set; do not use ±X/±Y/±Z axes and do not create any directly opposite pair of large lobes. Orient the final object so the projection resembles the source: one lobe projects upward, one lower-right, and two lower-left/back/front with visible depth separation. Each final large lobe extends from the central atom about 1.05 to 1.20 units along its tetrahedral vector, maximum radius about 0.28, yellow-orange #f5b041; each small rear lobe extends only about 0.28 to 0.35 units along the opposite direction, pale blue #79aee3. If the angle guide is enabled, draw a thin dashed gray tetrahedron connecting the four large-lobe tips and show one to three visible 109.5° labels near arcs between representative direction pairs; all six pairwise directions are 109.471° even if not all labels are displayed.
plan.notes: Render orbitals as smooth ellipsoid or teardrop meshes, not as flat icons. The final tetrahedral arrangement should be built from normalized vector directions and then transformed as one rigid group, so the 109.471° separations are preserved while the projection matches the textbook view. Use label sprites or CSS2D labels with depth-aware offsets; p-axis labels should have collision-free fixed offsets rather than being attached exactly at lobe tips. In Full sequence mode, show all groups and both arrows; in the other view modes, fade or hide nonselected groups while keeping the camera framing stable. Use cylinders plus cones for the Hybridization and downward arrows so their shaft length and thickness are visibly source-like. The angle guide should be toggled independently and should not distort the tetrahedral geometry.
